title: All Paths from Source Lead to Destination
summary: Given a directed graph with edges defined by [ai, bi], and nodes source and destination, determine if every path starting from source ends at destination.
statement: Given a directed graph with edges defined by [ai, bi], and nodes source and destination, determine if every path starting from source ends at destination. Conditions include the existence of at least one path from source to destination, no outgoing edges from destination, and a finite number of paths from source to destination. Return true if all paths from source lead to destination.
constraints: The directed graph may contain cycles.
Every maximal path from source must terminate at destination.
hints: A valid path cannot reach a wrong sink or a cycle.
Use three-state DFS: unseen, visiting, and proven safe.
A leaf is valid only at destination; revisiting a visiting node is a cycle; mark safe after all children pass.
Every maximal continuation is checked, while memoized safe nodes avoid repeated work.
editorial: Every maximal continuation is checked, while memoized safe nodes avoid repeated work.
